How Queen Victoria's Servants Made Christmas (1848) | History for Sleep

About 3 hours 5 min · Released Mon 23 Nov 2026 · Updated 22 Nov 2026 · narrated slowly for sleep

Watch on YouTube Listen on YouTube Music

Victorian Christmas history for sleep: Christmas 1848 below stairs at Windsor Castle with Queen Victoria's servants, the Great Kitchen and the royal trees.

In the Great Kitchen at Windsor Castle, a baron of beef turns before the fire for hours on Christmas Eve, while upstairs the royal trees are hung with gilt gingerbread and wax tapers. Tonight we'll spend Christmas 1848 below stairs, from the first cold candle before dawn to the quiet days that follow.

🌙 NO AD BREAKS: no mid-video ads, nothing to wake you.

The castle, the Great Kitchen, the baron of beef, the royal Christmas trees, the Queen's journal and the Illustrated London News engraving are historical. The young housemaid you walk with is a composite, drawn from the records of the women who worked in royal and great-house service in the 1840s.

About this sleep story

About 3 hours 5 min, narrated slowly for sleep, with no ad breaks. Made as history to fall asleep to: it's fine to drift off partway, and the chapters below let you find your place again.

This story follows one long Christmas at Windsor in 1848, from a cold attic before dawn on Christmas Eve, down through the Great Kitchen and the Long Corridor, to the trees, the candles, supper in the servants' hall, Christmas morning, a walk in the frost, a letter home, and the castle going quiet.

Sources

Researched and written for this channel from these sources. Where historians disagree, the narration says so.

  • Queen Victoria's journals (Royal Archives): Christmas Eve 1832 and Christmas 1848 at Windsor, the presents, the trees and the household
  • The Illustrated London News, Christmas Supplement, 23 December 1848: the engraving of the royal family's Christmas tree at Windsor
  • Royal Collection Trust: Christmas at Windsor and the Great Kitchen
  • Helen Rappaport, on Prince Albert's Christmas trees from Coburg and Windsor Great Park
  • World History Encyclopedia: the baron of beef, the boar's head, plum pudding, mince pies, and the trees kept until Twelfth Night
